commits.subject: fix(cli): check-results — shadow reconcile on every exit, wait loop, stale-scoring guard
commits.body:
The 2026-07-10 shadow pick sat ungraded for a month: SF@COL (10:15pm ET
first pitch) was not final at the 01:00 cron, the production-pending path
returned before attempting shadow reconciliation, and nightly runs grade
--date yesterday only — old dates are never revisited (the 02:00 reconcile
job rechecks terminal picks only).

Wait-not-sweep design (Eric), hardened by a Codex adversarial round:

- Every exit path (no-pick, already-resolved, unscoreable, resolver error,
  production-pending, stale-refused) attempts shadow reconciliation +
  status write first. Shadow grading is production-independent by design.
- --wait-deadline-et HH:MM (cron passes 06:00): retry the grading pass
  in-process every --wait-interval-min (15, IntRange 1-120) minutes until
  the grader itself reports everything settled. The grader's resolvability
  is the "day over" signal — suspended/postponed/batter-not-found
  semantics stay defined in resolve_daily_slot_results, where a schedule
  scan would deadlock on multi-day suspensions. Hard deadline: the final
  sleep is capped so no attempt STARTS after it. The fail-closed
  vanished-file branch stays pending (the file may be restored tonight).
- Stale-scoring guard (review blocker): update_streak applies results
  against CURRENT streak state, so grading an old date's unresolved
  production out of chronological order corrupts the streak — and nothing
  previously prevented it. Dates older than 2 days now refuse
  streak-bearing scoring (shadow still reconciles — what makes manual
  old-date remediation safe); --allow-stale-scoring overrides, only for a
  chronologically-ordered backfill. Existing scoring-mechanics tests opt
  in explicitly via the flag.

commits.subject: feat(health): result_resolution — stranded shadow AND production results alert instead of rotting
commits.body:
Backstop for what the check-results wait loop cannot cover: box down
overnight, multi-day suspensions, deadline exhausted on transient API
failures. Nothing else revisits a stranded date — nightly crons grade
yesterday only and reconcile skips nonterminal picks.

Review-driven shape: version-blind shadow scan (a v3 stack bump must not
hide stranded v2 results) inside a 30-day horizon (ancient
pre-discipline files never produce a standing alert); the production
side flags scoreable picks left unresolved (GH #144 unscoreable
previews stay silent); WARN at age >=2d reaches the attention DM
immediately (always-attention source), CRITICAL at >=7d; one
incident_key per date+side; runs unconditionally in the runner (gating
on shadow_model_enabled would stop monitoring already-written files the
moment generation is disabled); unresolved state derives in-memory from
the pick files, not the status JSON another process writes.

Also: write_manifest_json now writes via tmp+atomic-replace — the wait
loop rewrites the status artifact repeatedly and a signal mid-write must
never leave a torn file.

commits.subject: chore(cron)+docs: wait-deadline + flock singleton on the 01:00 grading cron
commits.body:
flock -n makes the possibly-hours-long grader a singleton (an
overlapping manual run no-ops instead of double-grading). ACTIVATION IS
MANUAL: deploys never touch crontab — run
`bash scripts/cron-setup-hetzner.sh install` on the box once (deploy
checklist). CLAUDE.md documents the protections, the safe remediation
path, and the deploy-window caveat (a deploy between 01:00-06:00 leaves
the old-code grader running; its status artifact stamps the new SHA).
